review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

19:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν Ἀπολλῶ εἶναι ἐν Κορίνθῳ Παῦλον διελθόντα τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εὑρεῖν τινας μαθητάς,
19:1.targetText: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "while".
τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ("the upper regions") is rendered the interior.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle διελθόντα (passed through) to the infinitive ἐλθεῖν (came); no Greek καί.
English opens the new sentence with the place, Ephesus.

19:2.targetText: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?”  “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

groups.note: πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") is rendered them.
In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
Ἀλλά here answers the question and is rendered No.
εἰ ("whether") is rendered that.

19:9.sourceText: ὡς δέ τινες ἐσκληρύνοντο καὶ ἠπείθουν κακολογοῦντες τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πλήθους, ἀποστὰς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀφώρισεν τοὺς μαθητάς, καθ’ ἡμέραν διαλεγόμενος ἐν τῇ σχολῇ Τυράννου.
19:9.targetText: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

groups.note: ἐσκληρύνοντο ("were hardened") is rendered stubbornly.
BSB folds the first two verbs into stubbornly refused to believe and uses this καί before maligned.

19:26.targetText: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.

19:34.sourceText: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων, ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κράζοντες Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
19:34.targetText: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

groups.note: The participle ἐπιγνόντες ("having recognized") is rendered as a when-clause.
φωνὴ … μία ("one voice") is rendered in unison.
ἐγένετο … κράζοντες ("arose … crying out") is rendered shouted; BSB's Greek text differs from N1904 by one word in this verse, without changing the sense.

19:35.sourceText: καταστείλας δὲ ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον φησίν Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι, τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς;
19:35.targetText: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

groups.note: δέ is rendered Finally, marking the next step.
γραμματεύς ("scribe", the town clerk) is rendered city clerk.
Ἐφέσιοι ("Ephesians") is rendered of Ephesus.
The rhetorical τίς ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς ("who of men is there who") is rendered everyone.
νεωκόρον ("temple keeper") is rendered guardian of the temple.
τοῦ διοπετοῦς ("the [image] fallen from heaven") is rendered of her image, which fell from heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: γάρ ("for") is not separately expressed in the question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle καταστείλας (quieted) to the main verb; no Greek καί.
English introduces what everyone knows with that.

19:36.sourceText: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν.
19:36.targetText: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.

19:40.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον, μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος, περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ἀποδοῦναι λόγον περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης. καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
19:40.targetText: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.
τῆς σήμερον ("the [matters] of today") is rendered today's events.
The genitive absolute μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος ("there being no cause") is recast as we have no justification.
BSB keeps the subject we of δυνησόμεθα ("we will be able") and folds the rest of the clause into have no justification to account.
ἀποδοῦναι λόγον ("to give an account") is rendered to account.
